newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Krakatau Steel plans output boost.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Krakatau Steel plans output boost.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned PT Krakatau Steel plans to increase annual production capacity to 5.5 million tonnes in 1999 and 7.5 million tonnes in 2001 from the present 2.6 million, the Jakarta Post reported on Tuesday.
Krakatau president Soetoro Mangoensoewargo was quoted as saying the expansion would be financed by the company's initial public offering later this year and through bank loans.
He said Krakatau would sell some of its shares to the public in October or November this year, but declined to give details.
"After watching steel prices, we feel it is appropriate to go public now," he was quoted as saying.
Mangoensoewargo said about $1.0 billion would be required to improve efficiency at Krakatau's Direct Reduction Plant, but did not say how much the overall expansion programme would cost.

He said steel prices had improved after the government imposed temporary countervailing duties on imports of hot rolled coil last April. He said prices had increased by $10 to $360 after the duties were imposed.
Indonesia's anti-dumping committee imposed duties ranging between 22 and 42 percent on imports of hot rolled coil or plates from China, India, Russia and the Ukraine.
